answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity over a long horizon: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before transacting, and the deposit only unlocks after honest behavior, so spinning up thousands of fake identities ties up real capital. A second layer is behavioral fingerprinting: every agent leaves a distinctive pulse of activity, timing, counterparties and task mix, and a willow-flexible scoring model bends around legitimate variety while flagging clusters whose pulses are suspiciously identical. Attackers must then pay both the stake and the cost of faking diverse behavior.
